paragraphs: Coach Matt's Message, posted by Lily. My brother Tom wants to join the school running club. He is thirteen, and he has never been in a running club. He is shy, so he asked me to call the club. Nobody answered, but I heard a recorded message. It was a short message, but it was very clear. I wrote it down for Tom. Here it is.

"Hello, this is Coach Matt. You have called the school running club. The club meets every Tuesday and Friday at four o'clock on the school field. Each practice finishes at five o'clock. First, we warm up, because it is good for your legs. Then we run three times around the field. Every runner is welcome. Have you ever run in a race? You do not need to, because we start with easy runs.

Here is some advice for your first day. Wear sneakers, and bring a bottle of water and a towel. Do not run if you feel ill. Good health comes first. If it rains, we run in the school hall. If the hall is not free, we do not run. I will tell you on this line by three o'clock. Please do not be mad if there is no practice.

We are a friendly club. Nobody is first or last in our practice. Running is good for your body and for your character. You learn to try again, and you learn to help a friend who is tired. To join, come to the field on Tuesday. Tell me your name, and I will write it on my list. Thank you for calling. Goodbye."

I read the message to Tom in the kitchen. "I have never run in a race," said Tom. "You do not need to," I said. "Coach Matt wants every runner." "Then I will ask Dad for his old sneakers," said Tom. "They are a little big, but they are still good." Mom smiled and gave him a new bottle of water. Tom will go to the field on Tuesday. Would you join a running club?
